source_citation: Yoon et al. (2016), An east-west contrast of upper ocean heat content variation south of the subpolar front in the East/Japan Sea, Journal of Geophysical Research: Oceans 121, 6418-6443, doi:10.1002/2016JC011891.
source_locator: Section 1, paragraphs beginning The TWC approaching and Part of the merged: Nearshore Branch from eastern channel to Tsugaru along Japanese coast; downstream merged branches do not preserve exclusive component identity.
route_scope: Japanese coastal-branch reference corridor from an OSW eastern Tsushima Strait approach to a western Tsugaru Strait approach. Excludes the offshore/Korean branch, Soya continuation and the separately named Tsugaru outflow. Connecting vertices do not assert uninterrupted flow or a full-system length. Downstream merges are shared circulation context, not exclusive nearshore water-parcel continuity.
classification_notes: Yoon et al. (2016) separates NB, OB and EKWC; Yokomatsu and Kida (2025) groups broader coastal and offshore pathways. Different grouping levels are not a settled universal branch count.
Downstream merging precludes exclusive water-parcel identity for the entire reference corridor.
Tsugaru and Soya are separately named outflows in Ohshima and Kuga (2023), not interchangeable Tsushima aliases.
JMA warns continuous paths are rare; reference vertices do not prove persistent connectivity.
JMA 100 m temperature-area strength index is not a current width, length or velocity-core footprint. No seasonal route or length extrema inferred.
